This mechanism has the property that the set of obtainable schools is fixed regardless of how I rank them—my ranking only determines which obtainable school I actually receive. This is characteristic of strategy-proof mechanisms like Deferred Acceptance (DA). In such mechanisms, truth-telling is a dominant strategy: since I cannot influence which schools are in my obtainable set, I should rank schools according to my true preferences to ensure I get the best one among those obtainable to me.

My true preference order is z > y > w > x. Since misrepresenting my preferences cannot expand my obtainable set (as stated), and truthful ranking guarantees I get my most preferred obtainable school, there is no strategic benefit to deviating from my true preferences. Submitting any other ranking risks getting a worse school within my obtainable set if I rank a less-preferred school higher.

Therefore, the optimal strategy is simply to submit my true preference ordering.
